Avatar V2 · integrated illustration system

Sixteen distinct saved facial identities, sixteen selectable outfits, eight illustrated age stages and independent skin, hairstyle, hair colour and clothing controls. All runtime artwork uses bundled full-colour PNG layers.

These are browser captures of the actual production screen and CharacterPortrait trees exported by React Native component tests. A CSS adapter lays out their native styles; routing, icons and hardware are mocked. They are rendered implementation evidence, not Android or iOS device screenshots. Native device visual and GPU performance checks remain unperformed because this environment has no simulator or attached device.

Registered layers preserve the full-colour illustration language, facial details and clothing variety. Head/ear/neck, hairstyles and clothing are separate authored assets. Skin and hair alternatives use continuous colour grading, without flat tint masks or palette quantisation. Legacy cheek and jaw contours remain compatible with saves; the face-shape controls have been removed from the appearance editor. Hair is fitted individually using each wig’s reference head and the measured outline of each face, contour and age. Long hairstyles remain continuous foreground layers drawn after the complete head and ears.

Implementation and verification scope

Existing four-field saves remain valid. Optional bounded appearance.identity metadata fixes the facial identity, and appearance.outfit saves an independent clothing choice. Legacy portraits derive their identity and default outfit from the existing person ID without rewriting save records. Creation drafts derive identity from the seed without advancing gameplay randomness. All portrait consumers continue using the same CharacterPortrait interface and shared rendering path.

Only local assets, image views, static SVG clipping and opacity are used at runtime. The existing react-native-svg dependency clips the illustrated skin to each garment opening. No network, new native dependency or per-frame pixel processing is used. Infants use one baby-head image; ages 3 and older use three to five image layers; each head atlas decodes to 1.03MiB. The sixteen-person adult grid references approximately 35MiB of unique decoded artwork. Bundled full-colour PNG files total approximately 105MiB, traded for portable rendering without a new native dependency. Artwork files are shared head/hair/shoulder/clothing layers, not complete portraits for every combination.

Automated coverage checks every one of the 1,966,080 identity/skin/face/hair/colour/clothing/age combinations, real creation controls, SQLite save/reload, legacy saves, accessible labels, and stable memoized drawings. Android and iOS exports validate asset bundling; browser captures do not establish native performance or device-specific image quality.
